purpose: Build and independently inspect a freestanding Rust successor to the synthetic arithmetic guest. No guest or resulting executable is run.

toolchain.download_trust: Official HTTPS release manifest and component SHA-256 checks. Retain manifest and archives; this is not an independently authenticated reproducible compiler or a host attestation.
toolchain.compiler_and_linker_execution: Only the host compiler, linker and offline analyzers execute. No output image is executed.

guest.image: ELF64 little-endian AArch64 ET_EXEC is an analysis container. The eventual guest payload is exactly the inspected .text bytes, loaded at a fixed address; no runtime ELF loader is added.

doorbell.pc: Derived from the linked epr_guest_doorbell symbol, never the baseline offset.

stack.initialization: Future host supplies a zeroed disjoint mapping; assembly sets SP before calling Rust.

guest.machine: Future EL1h with DAIF masked, baseline SCTLR_EL1 0x30d00800, no MMU/cache, no assumed FP/SIMD/SVE/LSE/PAC enablement. Current host is not upgraded by this build.
guest.sections: One RX .text load segment may contain read-only constants. .data/.bss/TLS/constructors/destructors/GOT/PLT are forbidden through zero-size linker assertions and independent ELF inspection. No unwind/runtime/dynamic imports or relocations remain.
guest.ownership: Assembly owns shared-memory reads, acquire/release, stack setup and deliberate fault. Rust receives four copied u64 values through the C ABI; it owns no host/guest pointers.
guest.rust_result_abi: One u64 in X0: 42 means the exact fixed request validated and checked addition succeeded; 0 means rejection. This private fixed-operation ABI has no generic request or command surface.
guest.publication: After checking Rust returned exactly 42, assembly reloads caller-clobbered pointers, writes reply ABI/sum/status, publishes sequence using STLR X4,[X1], DSB SY, then STR W4,[X3] at the unmapped doorbell.
guest.rejection: Unexpected Rust result branches to a named BRK before any reply publication. Panic has a distinct named BRK. If any trap is unexpectedly resumed, a local branch loop prevents fallthrough; future host must never resume.

build_and_inspection.source_snapshots: Two separately copied and hash-compared source sets in disjoint retained A/B directories, not one reused compiler output.
build_and_inspection.path_stability: Relative source/linker paths, fixed crate metadata, remapped source prefixes, no debug info, static relocation model, no build id, no incremental state or Cargo build scripts.
minimum_comparison: Map, disassembly, section, symbol and relocation observations
static_acceptance: Entry exactly code base; single RX load segment and no unexpected allocated content
No unresolved symbol, dynamic dependency, TLS or residual relocation
Stack initialized and bounded before Rust call; no recursion or runtime calls
All machine instructions inspected for baseline support and intended control flow
Doorbell opcode and release/barrier prefix match the frozen assembly contract
Compile-time positive/rejection assertions pass without executing an output binary
Independent bounded ELF parser rejects malformed and mutated inputs
build_and_inspection.retention: Retain source snapshots, exact invocation/environment, compiler/analyzer identities, stdout/stderr, ELF/map/disassembly, extracted image, inspections and comparisons. Failures remain recorded; ordinary development successor builds use new directories.
build_and_inspection.limits: Build reproducibility and static inspection are not execution correctness, continuous host integrity, VM attestation, energy measurement or authority closure.

before_any_later_boot: Independently review the final image and successor-specific host/receipt integration
Add the separate stack mapping and exact new image/trap/machine-state checks
Pass pure verifier positive and negative tests
Retain signed host identity and use an explicitly scoped synthetic development invocation
